Actual Article Body:
I can't quit ... yet!

Welcome to your new favorite advice column from your favorite feminist journalism collective! New editions are published every Wednesday. Read on for the drama, the tea, and the commiseration—and if you want to submit a question, scroll on down to the bottom of this post for more info.

Let's get into it:

Dear Butter,

Andrea, here. What a delightfully, lightfully evil question! Here are a few of my go-tos for when people have lost the plot but I can't simply walk away:

You can find Flytrap posters, tees, trucker hats, and more at our merch store! Including our brand new rainbow "fuck the algorithm, fuck AI" shirt!!

All profits in September and October from our charity bandana designed by our Art Director rommy torrico will be going to Gaza Soup Kitchen.

I also asked Flytrap cofounder s.e. smith to weigh in with some zingers, and they obliged:

Sounds like it's time to quiet quit, comrade! Do the least, with zest (and plausible deniability) followed closely by malicious compliance. And if there are ANY benefits you can milk, please do: All the sick time, all the personal days, max out your office stipend, all the professional development $$$, and remember to clock out at five on the dot and turn your phone/laptop off until 9am on the next business day.

The weaponized "Okay." (with period) followed by NOTHING ELSE is a classic for a reason! Depending on norms at your workplace, the lowercase "okay." can be even more pointed (if you're in Slack, for example, I know that in some companies people don't necessarily capitalize all the time so this is something no one can really call you on). Similarly for "got it, will do," "acknowledging receipt," and "thanks for the update." And as a person who becomes apoplectic about emoji responses to emails because this isn't a group chat and I don't need a "Butter Wouldn't Melt reacted 👍 to your message" email ... start using emoji reacts liberally.

"Could you say that again? I want to make sure I understand?" is a great one, even better if they say something absolutely wild and you can do the "I just want to double-check: You're saying you don't want me to sanitize the ice cream scoops at the end of my shift?"

Ultimately, what you really want to do here obviously is go off on these people and it can be really nice to think about doing that, but getting stuck in that place isn't good for you. Instead of thinking about this as "How do I let these people know they're awful?" think about "How do I care less" and "How do I seek validation outside of work so my frustration and anger don't take up all of my brain?"— s.e. smith

Readers, do y'all have any devastatingly polite burns for our letter-writer? Leave them some advice in the comments!

Submit your queries about life, love, and everything else, and a Flytrap co-owner (probably Andrea, aka the Bad Advisor, though we'll float questions to the entire collective and find the right person for the job) will tell you what the fuck is up.

Submissions must be under 500 words, and while we can't guarantee we'll answer every letter, for those we do: we'll give you the best ideas we have about whatever the hell is going on with you. (Caveat, etc: we are not therapists, lawyers, accountants, actuaries, psychics, coaches, doctors, or anything besides a whole bunch of people who have lived through a bunch of nonsense.) If for some reason the submission form doesn't work, holler at us: advice@theflytrapmedia.com

Please remember that every submission has the potential to be published; we'll remove identifying details as we're able. Don't blow up your own spot, but please give us the goss.
